items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What about Willie Warner and Frank Lewis? Did you know that? ... [INTERVIEWEE] They played all that music.

ctx.x: The youngster or the father? No, the youngster.
Would he make growls and all that? Yeah. What about Willie Warner and Frank Lewis? Did you know that? Well yeah. What did they play like? Did they play like Big R or did they play like Tio?

They played all that music. It's more in parts I think. It's a musician, you know? Mm-hmm. They worked as a musician. It didn't work as a musician. It didn't work as a musician. Like I would work. You wouldn't call him hot? Well he was all right.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-12-20
items.q: I don't remember nothing about that. I don't know nothing about that.

ctx.x: It ain't right. But sometimes you take clarinet to it, you got three or four clarinets.

Well the reason why I ask you that is, there's an old photograph of Bolden's band, where he has Frank Lewis and Willie Warner both in the photograph, both with the clarinets. And I wondered if that was the reason, if they ever did have two clarinets in the band, one playing lead, one playing the lead.

Well I don't remember nothing about that. I don't know nothing about that. And I know plenty of musicians and music too. You see I don't say I know music, but I know some of them. You certainly know more than most people. Yeah, but in the meantime for clarinets to do that, they can put two clarinets together. But a clarinet is supposed to use a cyclic one.
